newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING Barings downgrades Egis EPS forecast.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings downgrades Egis EPS forecast.

text.p: ING Barings downgraded its 1997 earnings per share (EPS) forecast to 811 forints from 882 forints earlier for Hungarian pharmaceuticals firm Egis Rt as higher marketing costs would reduce margins.
However, ING Barings said in the May issue of its "Eastern European Monthly Review" that it maintained its "long-term buy" rating on shares of Egis, a company majority-owned by France's Servier S.A.

"We expect sales growth of 21.5 percent at Egis as opposed to 33.1 percent at (peer industrial) Richter," ING Barings said. "In addition Egis still has to invest heavily in marketing and distribution this year (a 60 percent increse in total marketing costs)."
In 1997 Egis plans to spend five billion to six billion on investment, research and development and marketing.
Egis is expected to underperform Richter in terms of EPS growth, the analysts said.
"Egis will barely be able to deliver real EPS growth in 1997, while Richter's real EPS growth could easily be 25 percent," ING Barings said.

ING Barings' equity analyst team said Egis was heading for a net profit of 6.3 billion forints in 1997 as against its previous forecast of 6.8 billion forints. In 1996 Egis had an after-tax profit of 5.6 billion forints.

In terms of sales growth Richter is expected to outperform Egis, whose management is aiming for "sustainable growth" this year and to increase its sales to around 30 billion in 1997 from 24.69 billion in 1996.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday Egis closed at 11,600 forints, up 400 and Richter at 14,900 forints, up 400.
